S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.title: Public Access Block is incomplete
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.what: One or more of the four S3 Public Access Block switches is off (or missing). The bucket can still be made public through an ACL or a bucket policy.
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.how: A PutBucketPublicAccessBlock call left BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, or RestrictPublicBuckets set to false — or the control was never applied after CreateBucket.
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.affects: Anyone on the internet can be granted list or read access without another engineer noticing. Student records, backups, or logs in the bucket become one policy change away from a public leak.
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.blast_radius: Account-wide data exposure, FERPA / PII disclosure, ransomware staging, and failed audits (CIS 2.1.4, FSBP S3.8).
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.remedy_does: ASPARe calls PutPublicAccessBlock and turns all four flags on. New public ACLs and public bucket policies are rejected.
S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS.remedy_leaves: Objects already copied off-account are not recalled. A separate public ACL finding is cleaned up by S3_REMOVE_PUBLIC_ACL.

S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.title: Bucket ACL grants public or every-AWS-user access
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.what: The bucket ACL includes AllUsers (everyone on the internet) or AuthenticatedUsers (any AWS account). That is a live public grant, not just a missing guardrail.
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.how: Someone applied a canned ACL such as public-read, or granted READ/WRITE to the global ACL groups. This only works when Public Access Block is also off.
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.affects: Anyone who can guess or enumerate the bucket URL can list or download objects. Search engines and scanners routinely find these buckets within hours.
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.blast_radius: Immediate public disclosure of every object the grant covers. Critical for FERPA, backups, and CI artifacts.
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.remedy_does: ASPARe replaces the ACL with a private owner-only grant (or equivalent) so AllUsers and AuthenticatedUsers disappear.
S3_PUBLIC_ACL_EXPOSURE.remedy_leaves: Public Access Block should also be enabled; otherwise the next PutBucketAcl can reopen the hole.

S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.title: No explicit default encryption
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.what: GetBucketEncryption did not return an approved default algorithm (AES256 or KMS). New objects do not inherit a reviewed customer encryption setting.
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.how: The bucket was created without PutBucketEncryption, or default encryption was deleted. AWS may still apply a platform baseline, but ASPARe requires an explicit, policy-approved configuration.
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.affects: Objects can land unencrypted-by-policy. Key rotation, KMS audit, and 'encryption at rest' evidence for compliance reviews are missing.
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.blast_radius: Failed CIS 2.1.1 / FSBP S3.4 checks and weaker protection if the account is later compromised.
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.remedy_does: ASPARe sets a default SSE rule (AES256 unless a KMS key is configured) so every new object inherits encryption.
S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED.remedy_leaves: Existing objects are not retroactively rewritten. Re-encrypt those separately if the policy requires it.

S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.title: HTTP (cleartext) access is still allowed
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.what: The bucket policy does not Deny requests where aws:SecureTransport is false. Clients can talk to S3 over plain HTTP.
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.how: No bucket policy exists, or the policy has no reviewed Deny for insecure transport covering the bucket ARN and object ARNs.
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.affects: Access keys, query strings, and object bytes can be intercepted on the network path. Internal tools that still use http:// silently keep working.
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.blast_radius: Credential theft and in-transit disclosure. Breaks CIS 2.1.2 / FSBP S3.5.
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.remedy_name: Enforce HTTPS in the bucket policy
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.remedy_does: ASPARe merges a reviewed Deny statement that blocks s3:* when aws:SecureTransport is false, without wiping unrelated policy statements.
S3_HTTPS_ENFORCEMENT_MISSING.remedy_leaves: Legitimate HTTPS clients are unchanged. HTTP-only scripts will start failing — that is the point.

S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.title: Object versioning is off
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.what: The bucket does not have versioning Status=Enabled. Overwrites and deletes replace the only copy of an object.
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.how: Versioning was never enabled, or it was suspended. This is common on lab and log buckets created with defaults.
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.affects: Ransomware, a bad deploy, or an accidental aws s3 rm can destroy data with no prior version to restore. Audit of who changed an object is weaker.
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.blast_radius: Data loss and longer recovery. Medium severity — ASPARe alerts and does not auto-enable it, because versioning changes cost and lifecycle behavior.
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.remedy_does: The action exists (PutBucketVersioning Enabled) but the risk policy keeps MEDIUM findings on ALERT_AND_LOG. An operator must opt in.
S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED.remedy_leaves: No automatic write is performed. Enable versioning in change control if the data class requires recoverability.
